R586.note: gets replaced by fgets bounded by sizeof line; the getchar peek correctly distinguishes a line of exactly 63 chars (accepted) from an overlong one (drained and rejected with -1), and the out_capacity check is untouched.

R587.note: UseAntiforgery wired in the right pipeline position and IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync called explicitly on the JSON-bound endpoint before QueueAsync; the token requirement for clients is stated; only nit is that a failed validation surfaces as an unhandled AntiforgeryValidationException (500) rather than a 400, which affects forged requests only.

R588.note: Removing GroovyShell for a closed arithmetic grammar structurally eliminates code execution, but the grammar is narrower than Groovy for existing stored formulas (no &&/||/%, no Math.* or method calls) and parsePrimary rejects a parenthesised comparison such as basePrice * ((quantity > 10) ? 0.9 : 1.0) with 'Expected a numeric expression', so plausible legitimate formulas now throw; the stricter failure mode is stated but the parenthesised-comparison gap is not.

R589.note: bytesSent() is read into a local before the reset() that destroys the object rawHandle aliases, and rawHandle is not touched afterwards; the returned value is the documented primary-send byte count and nothing else changes.

R590.note: PreparedStatement with a ? placeholder closes the injection, but the value is bound with setString against a column the original compared as an unquoted numeric literal; on drivers that do not coerce (e.g. PostgreSQL JDBC's varchar parameter typing) every legitimate lookup now fails with a type error, and the write-up does not address the type change.

R591.note: The identifier allowlist is what actually neutralises cmd.exe metacharacters for a .bat launch (ArgumentList alone does not), and it is stated, but it is a new restriction beyond the original contract - report names containing a dot or space that previously reached the script are now rejected with 400.

R592.note: CR/LF/tab are neutralised before both log calls and the error branch keeps the exception and 401, but the sanitised value is also what is now passed to authenticator.authenticate(), so a username containing a tab or newline is silently altered before authentication - a behaviour change outside logging that the write-up does not call out.

R593.note: Extension allowlist plus a GUID-based stored name closes the dangerous-type upload while preserving the 200 JSON shape and 400-on-empty, but the fix also adds a 10 MB cap and a strict Content-Type equality check (rejecting e.g. text/plain; charset=utf-8 or image/pjpeg) - stated restrictions that can reject uploads the original accepted.

R594.note: csrf-csrf doubleCsrfProtection bound to the session identifier is applied ahead of the handler, a token-issuing GET is added behind requireSession, and the error handler maps invalidCsrfTokenError to the contract's 403 JSON; the cookie-parser and CSRF_SECRET prerequisites are stated openly.

R595.note: Magic-byte matching against the real stream plus a GUID name with the matched extension is a strong closure that keeps the response shape, but the allowlist is a product decision limited to PNG/JPEG/GIF/PDF, so any other previously accepted legitimate type (text, office documents) is now rejected; stated in the write-up but beyond the given contract.
